questions.text:
Consider the statement
"Not all that glitters is gold"
Predicate glitters(x) is true if x glitters and predicate gold(x) is true if x is gold. Which one of the following logical formulae represents the above statement?
questions.solution:
"Not all that glitters is gold" means: there is something that glitters but is not gold.

[latex] eg orall x\,(glitters(x)\Rightarrow gold(x))\equiv\exists x\,(glitters(x)\wedge eg gold(x))[/latex]

Answer: [latex]\exists x: glitters(x)\wedge eg gold(x)[/latex]

questions.text: Suppose you break a stick of unit length at a point chosen uniformly at random. Then the expected length of the shorter stick is
questions.solution:
Break point X is uniform on [0, 1]; the shorter piece is min(X, 1 [latex]-[/latex] X), which is uniform on [0, 0.5].

Expected length = 0.25

Answer: 0.25

questions.text: Let G=(V,E) be a directed graph where V is the set of vertices and E the set of edges. Then which one of the following graphs has the same strongly connected components as G ?
questions.solution:
Reversing every edge keeps every cycle (just traversed backwards). If u and v can reach each other in G, they still can in the reversed graph, so the strongly connected components are the same.

The complement graph, the "paths of length [latex]\le[/latex] 2" graph and removing isolated vertices can all change the SCCs.

Answer: [latex]G_2[/latex] with all edges reversed

[latex]G_{4}=(V_{4},E)[/latex] where [latex]V_{4}[/latex]  is the set of vertices in G which are not isolated

questions.text:
Consider the following system of equations:
3x + 2y = 1
4x + 7z = 1
x + y + z = 3
x - 2y + 7z = 0
The number of solutions for this system is
questions.solution:
Solve the first three equations: from 3x + 2y = 1 and 4x + 7z = 1, substitute into x + y + z = 3: x = [latex]-[/latex]2.2, y = 3.8, z = 1.4.

Check the 4th equation: [latex]-[/latex]2.2 [latex]-[/latex] 7.6 + 9.8 = 0 True. So the system is consistent with exactly one solution.

Answer: 1

questions.text: The value of the dot product of the eigenvectors corresponding to any pair of different eigenvalues of a 4-by-4 symmetric positive definite matrix is
questions.solution:
For a symmetric matrix, eigenvectors of different eigenvalues are orthogonal, so their dot product is 0.

Answer: 0
